criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The mission rationale is articulated exceptionally well. The primary purpose (fluid lensing for coral reef monitoring), rationale for a single spacecraft, and relevant Australian operators/stakeholders (CSIRO, BOM) are all clearly identified and justified.

evidence.quote: A newer technology called fluid lensing has been used in combination with AI analysis to detect colour/tone changes to the seafloor
Thus, only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications, reduces cost
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?

criteria.reasoning: The conclusion provides an appropriate summary drawn directly from the mission analysis, accurately reflecting launch risks, orbit selection, and ground station capability for Great Barrier Reef monitoring.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Formatting lacks professional polish. Figures and tables lack formal captions and numbering. Tables copied from Wikipedia retain raw footnote hyperlinks ([50], [67]). References consist solely of bare URLs, include broken formatting, and explicitly cite Wikipedia contrary to instructions.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Incomplete sentence cut off mid-thought: 'utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable'.
No ballistic coefficient, drag area, or orbit decay calculations provided to demonstrate that the drag sail can deorbit from 600 km within the 25-year standard.
Flight manifest tables are raw copy-pastes from Wikipedia with orphaned citation markers.

overall: A well-conceived mission with strong Australian relevance and solid STK orbit/access analysis. However, report presentation is hindered by uncaptioned figures, incomplete sentences, bare URLs, raw copied Wikipedia tables, and using Wikipedia as a source.

feedback.summary: You presented an innovative, well-justified mission concept using fluid lensing for coral reef monitoring, supported by solid STK orbit and ground access analyses. Your rationale and conclusions align well with Australian stakeholder needs. To reach higher rubric levels, ensure your technical design includes rigorous calculations (such as drag sail deorbit sizing) and improve report presentation by eliminating raw website copy-pastes, adding formal figure captions, and using standard reference formatting.

criteria.C1: You achieved Accomplished by clearly articulating the mission's primary purpose, stakeholder relevance (CSIRO, BOM), and rationale for a single spacecraft in the Introduction. Detailed descriptions and relevant Australian context were presented to a high standard.
criteria.C2: You reached Adequate by defining core elements like the 600 km SSO orbit and Mt Pleasant station with STK access data. To reach Accomplished, provide derived calculations instead of external curves, size your drag sail with orbital decay calculations in Mission Duration & EOL, and complete cut-off sentences.
criteria.C3: You achieved Accomplished by synthesizing key mission outcomes effectively in the Conclusion. You drew balanced, specific conclusions regarding your chosen orbit, ground station pass durations, and launch vehicle risks associated with the Vega E.
criteria.C4: You reached Adequate as the core report structure was identifiable. To achieve Accomplished, format references formally instead of using bare URLs, avoid citing Wikipedia, number and caption all figures and tables, and replace copied tables with clean, self-authored technical summaries.

next_steps: Perform explicit orbital decay or ballistic coefficient hand calculations in 'Mission Duration & EOL' to verify the drag sail meets the 25-year deorbit requirement from 600 km.
Synthesize flight manifest data into your own original, cleanly formatted comparative trade tables rather than copying raw tables with external hyperlinks.
Standardize presentation by numbering and captioning all figures and adopting a standard academic referencing style (e.g., IEEE) without bare URLs or Wikipedia citations.
